questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

No truck is a bus.

Some buses are cars.

**Conclusions:**

I. No bus is a truck.

II. All cars are trucks.

III. Some cars are buses.

options.text: Conclusions I, II and III follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

We draw a Venn diagram from the given statements:

No truck is a bus.

Some buses are cars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12bbab03d7c6e29b9de4d6ccbbdbf8954dee165ec0d52764c2e01fd38211b374.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

**I. No bus is a truck ****→ Follows** → We have 'no truck is a bus' so it is clear that bus and truck is not related and it is safe to say that no bus is a truck, therefore the conclusion follows.

**II. All cars are trucks ****→ Does not follow** → From the statements, 'no truck is a bus' and 'some buses are cars' so there will be some cars that will only be bus and not truck which means not all cars are trucks thus the conclusion does not follow.

**III. Some cars are buses → ****Follows** → Since 'some buses are cars', it is direct that some cars will definitely be buses so the conclusion follows.

So **both conclusions I and III follows.**

**Hence, the correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: If 2 March 2022 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was it on 2 March 2006?

We apply Keller's rule which says:

F = k + [(13 × m - 1)/5] + D + [D/4] + [c/4] - 2 × c , where

k is the day of the month.

m is the month number.

D is the last two digits of the year.

c is the first two digits of the year.

So we put the values as:

k = 2 ; m = 1(march=1) ; D = 06 ; c = 20

Now we substitute the values and solve the equation: (Ignore all decimal)

F = 31 + __[(13×1-1)/5]__ + 6 + __[6/4]__ + __[20/4]__ - 2 × 20

F = 31 + 2 + 6 + 1 + 5 - __2 × 20__

F = __31 + 2 + 6 + 1 + 5__ - 40 

F = __45 - 40__

F = 5 

5 means Thursday.

Therefore, 2 March 2006 was a Thursday.

**Hence, the correct answer is option 3.**

• **Battle of Haldighati:**

 
 
• The Battle of Haldighati was a battle fought on 18 June 1576 between the armies of the Rana of Mewar, Maharana Pratap, and the Mughal emperor Akbar’s forces, led by Man Singh I of Amber.
 
• Although the battle ended in defeat for the forces of Mewar, Maharana Pratap escaped continuing his valiant resistance against the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Buxar:**
 
 
• The Battle of Buxar took place in 1764, in the town of Buxar in present-day Bihar, India. It was a significant battle fought during the British East India Company's expansion in India.
 
• The British East India Company, led by Major Hector Munro, faced a coalition of Indian rulers consisting of the Nawab of Oudh, Shuja-ud-Daula, the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, and the forces of the ruler of Mir Qasim.
 
• The battle was the outcome of the misuse of Farman and Dastak, and also the trade expansionist aspiration of the English.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• The Hindu ruler Samrat Hem Chandra Vikramaditya, often known as Hemu, governed North India from Delhi, and the army of Akbar fought the Second Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is an overlapping membranous sac with ER-like thickness that helps in processing and packaging protein and lipid molecules, especially stable proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golgi apparatus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Golgi Apparatus:**__

__
 
• The Golgi apparatus has multiple names such as the **Golgi complex or Golgi body.**
 
• The name is given on the name of the scientist, who discovered the organelle, i.e. Camillo Golgi.
 
• It is **found in all the eukaryotic cells**, plants as well as animals.
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles present in the cytosol of the cell.
 
• The Golgi body comprises 5 to 8 cup-shaped, series of compartments known as **cisternae**. Cisternae is a flattened, disk-shaped, stacked pouches that make up the Golgi apparatus. A Golgi stack mostly contains 4 to 8 cisternae. However, ~60 cisternae are found in some protists. A mammalian cell contains ~40 to 100 stacks of cisternae.
 
• Animal cells generally contain around 10 to 20 Golgi stacks per cell, which are connected by tubular connections.
 
• Golgi complex is mostly found near the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a66665c8b7d6a84497438e44c0511f463d9d862ee49c9ea1be606ed25af9562.png] 

**Functions of Golgi Bodies:**__

 
• Its main function is the **packaging and secretion of proteins.** 
 
• It receives proteins from Endoplasmic Reticulum. It packages it into **membrane-bound vesicles**, which are then transported to various destinations, such as lysosomes, plasma membrane or secretion.
 
• They also take part in the** transport of lipids **and the formation of lysosomes.
 
• **Post-translational modification and enzymatic processing** occur near the membrane surface in Golgi bodies, e.g. phosphorylation, glycosylation, etc.
 
• Golgi apparatus is the site for the synthesis of various glycolipids, sphingomyelin, etc.
 
• In the plant cells,** complex polysaccharides of the cell wall** are synthesised in the Golgi apparatus.

questions.question: If the LCM of two numbers a and b is 60 and their HCF is 15. Determine their mean proportion.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The product of two numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF.

Product = 60 × 15 = 900

Mean proportion of two numbers is the square root of their product.

Mean proportion = √900 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of a and b = 60

HCF of a and b = 15

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43a908ea2dc7e88b431deb67ade97f86de828182f291f2df087497ee9065b396.png]

Product of two numbers (a × b) = LCM × HCF

⇒ a × b = 60 × 15

⇒ a × b = 900

⇒ Mean Proportion = √(a × b)

⇒ Mean Proportion = √900

⇒ Mean Proportion = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportion

The mean proportion between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportion

The third proportion of two numbers a and b is a value c such that a : b = b : c, which gives c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportion

The fourth proportion of three numbers a, b, and c is a value d such that a : b = c : d, which gives d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Product Rule of Numbers

For any two positive integers, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM.

questions.question: If the number 476**0 is divisible by both 3 and 11, then in the hundredth and tenth places, the non-zero digits are, respectively:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For divisibility by **3**, the sum of digits (4 + 7 + 6 + x + y + 0 = 17 + x + y) must be a multiple of 3.

For divisibility by **11**, the difference of sums of alternate digits (x + 7 + 0) − (y + 6 + 4) = x − y − 3 must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Testing Option (4) where **x = 8** and **y = 5**:

Sum = 17 + 8 + 5 = 30, which is divisible by 3. Difference = 8 − 5 − 3 = 0, which is divisible by 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 and 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number is 476xy0, where x is at the **hundredth** place and y is at the **tenth** place.

**Divisibility by 3:** Sum of digits = 4 + 7 + 6 + x + y + 0 = 17 + x + y.

**Divisibility by 11:** (Sum of digits at odd places) − (Sum of digits at even places) = 0 or 11n.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6d76cc3b87dbdf6bc9af1a1e01055baa8452dc4d0e0b1475f6486ab095891f5.png] 

⇒ Sum of odd positions (from right) = 0 + x + 7 = 7 + x

⇒ Sum of even positions (from right) = y + 6 + 4 = 10 + y

⇒ Difference = (10 + y) − (7 + x) = y − x + 3

⇒ For divisibility by 11: y − x + 3 = 0 or 11

⇒ Case 1: x − y = 3

⇒ From options, if x = 8 and y = 5, then 8 − 5 = 3 (Satisfied)

⇒ Sum of digits check: 17 + 8 + 5 = 30 (Multiple of 3, Satisfied)

**∴ The correct answer is 8 and 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the **absolute difference** between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Combined Divisibility

If a number is divisible by both 3 and 11, it is also divisible by **33** (since 3 and 11 are co-primes).</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **CSA** of 3 such cones = 3 × 60π = 180π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 180π cm².**

questions.question: A retailer wants to sell an item for Rs. 2,700 after granting a 10% discount. What is the marked price of the item?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A 10% **discount** means the item is sold at 90% of its **Marked Price**.

90% of Marked Price = ₹2,700

1% of Marked Price = 2,700 ÷ 90 = 30

100% (Marked Price) = 30 × 100 = ₹3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = ₹2,700

**Discount Percentage** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 − Discount %]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca0a1d4586eb62810420f98df5c24975ad9ccda848a514ceb6ecfc2faaef1aea.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be MP.

⇒ MP = [2,700 × 100] ÷ [100 − 10]

⇒ MP = [2,700 × 100] ÷ 90

⇒ MP = 30 × 100

⇒ MP = ₹3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the product label. It is the base for calculating the discount.

Selling Price (SP)

The final price paid by the customer after the discount is deducted: SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage

The reduction offered on the Marked Price: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Markup Percentage

The percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price: Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

He was enough tall / to be admitted / into the armed forces.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "He was enough tall". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Enough means 'as much as necessary'.
 
• It can be used with an adjective, an adverb, a verb or a noun. It can also act as a pronoun.
 
 
• **With adjectives and adverbs : enough comes after adjectives and adverbs**.
 
 
• For example: I'm not tall enough to reach the top shelf.
 
• For example: Your marks are good enough to study engineering at university.
 
 
 
 
 
• From the above explanation it can be concluded that the correct sentence is: He was tall enough to be admitted into the armed forces. 

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• With verbs: enough comes after verbs.
 
 
• For example: I make sure I drink enough during the day.
 
 
 
• With nouns: enough comes before nouns.
 
 
• For example: There isn't enough bread to make sandwiches.
 
 
 
• As a pronoun: enough can also be used without a noun. 
 
 
• For example: I'll get some more chairs. There aren't enough.
 
 
 
• With an adjective and a noun: When enough is used with an adjective and a noun, two positions are possible but the meaning changes.
 
 
• We haven't got big enough envelopes. 
 
• We haven't got enough big envelopes.
 
 
 
• When enough is after the adjective (big enough envelopes), it describes the adjective – the envelopes are too small.
 
• When enough is before the adjective (enough big envelopes), it describes the noun phrase – we have some big envelopes, but we need more.
